ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There is one main node on each of the left and right sides in the figure. The upper branch from the left node to the right node is, in sequence, a 1 F capacitor and a 1 H inductor connected in series; the middle branch is a 1 Ω resistor directly connected across between the left and right nodes; the lower branch contains a 1 Ω resistor and an AC voltage source, and the voltage source is labeled as (1.0 sin t) V. The direction of the current i(t) is marked on the vertical wire on the left side. Reasoning: From the source label (1.0 sin t) V, it can be known that the angular frequency \omega=1 rad/s. Using phasor impedance representation, the upper-branch capacitor impedance Z_C=1/(j\omega C)=1/(j·1·1)=-j Ω, and the inductor impedance Z_L=j\omega L=j·1·1=j Ω. Therefore, the total series impedance of the upper branch Z_C+Z_L=-j+j=0, which is equivalent to the left and right nodes being short-circuited by this LC branch. The voltage between the left and right nodes is zero, so the voltage across the middle 1 Ω resistor is zero. The lower-branch source and the lower 1 Ω resistor form a loop through this short circuit, and the peak value of the voltage source is 1.0 V, so the peak current is I_m=1.0/1=1 A. The RMS value of the sinusoidal current is I_{rms}=I_m/\sqrt{2}=1/\sqrt{2} A.

method.method_draft: Assign the right node as reference and let V be the phasor voltage of the left node. The top series LC branch has impedance jωL+1/(jωC)=j-j=0 at ω=1, so finite circuit behavior requires V=0; equivalently, the two nodes are clamped together.
